finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into the SQL string through an f-string. The unauthenticated attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run UNION-based queries to read any table in shop.db.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: Route /search has no auth decorator or middleware
term taken from query string with no validation
term placed directly in the SQL text via an f-string, not a bound parameter
Query rows are returned as JSON, so UNION SELECT output is exfiltrated to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No validation, escaping, allowlist or parameter binding on term. The sibling handlers at app.py:18 and app.py:25 use ? placeholders, so this is the only handler that skips them. No auth in the app. sqlite3 execute() rejects stacked statements, so the impact is limited to read access (UNION, e.g. against sqlite_master and other tables).

verdict.reason: app.py:11-12 puts request.args 'q' straight into the SQL text through an f-string, with no auth decorator at app.py:9 and no validation or binding, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so a UNION injection is exploitable by an anonymous user (the siblings at app.py:18 and :25 do use ? placeholders).
